topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the introductory framing and objectives for the lecture on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Innate immune recognition of infection and tissue damage
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the molecular mechanisms by which the innate immune system senses pathogens and damage using pattern recognition receptors, toll-like receptors, and inflammasomes.

topics.label: Inflammatory response, leukocyte recruitment, and systemic consequences
topics.groupedBecause: They describe how sentinel cells initiate local and systemic inflammation, orchestrate leukocyte extravasation into tissues, and interact with the lymphatic system.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: They address how inflammatory responses are resolved, how damaged tissue is repaired, and the causes and protective adaptations of chronic inflammation.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next topic
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming topic on the complement system.
